Thought: I need to determine what the hazard statement H227 means in chemistry. Hazard statements are standardized phrases used in the Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals (GHS) to describe the hazards of chemical products. Each hazard statement has a unique code starting with the letter H followed by three digits.

I need to identify which of the given options correctly defines H227.

H227 is a hazard statement that refers to "Combustible liquid" in the GHS system. This is used for liquids with flash points between 60°C and 93°C, which can burn but are not as easily ignited as flammable liquids.

Looking at the options:
A. Combustible liquid - This matches the definition of H227
B. Flammable gas - This would be a different hazard statement
C. May be fatal if swallowed and enters airways - This is an aspiration hazard statement
D. May cause harm to breast-fed children - This is a reproductive toxicity hazard statement
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
